prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active forms of GLP-1 that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B042 first, but unanimity is not itself merit, so I restate the scientific case. The chain from proglucagon processing, to identification of the insulinotropic GLP-1(7-36) form, to the human physiology of the incretin effect, to receptor biology and then to long-acting agonists is unusually complete and unusually well tested. It has been confirmed independently over decades, including by large randomized outcome trials, and it has changed how type 2 diabetes and obesity are treated, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery is a physiological finding about a gut hormone, which fits the prize's remit squarely. A single-achievement prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov credits the basic hormone biology and peptide identification on which the therapeutics rest.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The three-person cap forces us to leave out Knudsen, whose design of liraglutide and semaglutide is what actually put the biology into patients, and the proglucagon and GLP-1 work of Habener and colleagues is not among the credited names at all, so priority between Mojsov and that group cannot be settled from the shortlist alone. A prize that omits the drug developers may look like it misses the clinical breakthrough, while one that includes Knudsen displaces a basic discoverer. There is also a risk that a topic this widely known will be treated as the default and receive less scrutiny than the lower-ranked candidates.

responses.point: Linnarsson proposed Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, arguing that the discovery arc from basic biology to therapy is best captured by including the person who designed liraglutide and semaglutide, and that Mojsov's early peptide work is a claim the cap cannot accommodate.
responses.response: I take the argument seriously but do not agree. Knudsen's work is a major medicinal-chemistry and development achievement, but the Nobel-level discovery is the identification of the active peptide and the physiology it acts through, without which the drug design would have had no target. Dropping Mojsov in favour of Knudsen would remove the person who identified the active GLP-1(7-36) form and would turn the prize into a drug-development award. I agree that Drucker and Holst are secure. Where I qualify my own position is that if the committee judges the active-peptide priority to be unresolved, Knudsen is the principled fallback for the third place, not Mojsov by default.

responses.point: Perlmann treated B042 as a clear, specific discovery with lasting impact, with a coherent Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio, and described Knudsen's contribution as drug engineering whose fair weight is contestable.
responses.response: I agree with his trio and with the distinction between physiological discovery and drug engineering. I would add that the strength of B042 over his rank-three choice, B015, is the breadth of the underlying physiology. Antisense splicing correction for SMA is a fine mechanism-to-bedside story, but it is a narrower discovery and the credited pair does not cover contributors such as Hua and Singh, whereas B042 rests on a physiological principle with effects across several organ systems.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius placed TNF blockade (B041) third and described it as a model of bench-to-bedside discovery that is arguably overdue, with Feldmann and Maini as a clean pair.
responses.response: The pair is indeed cleaner than most, and I accept that B041 is mature and overdue. My hesitation, which I would like her to address, is that the finding that TNF drives synovial inflammation was followed by antibody engineering and trials shaped by many contributors, so I need to understand what the single Nobel-level discovery is beyond the demonstration of clinical efficacy. I did not rank B041 in my opening eight, and I would keep it below B038 and B029 unless the case can be made on originality rather than clinical success.

responses.point: El Manira ranked optogenetics (B029) second, stressing its originality and its transformation of circuit analysis, while accepting that six credited names exceed the cap and any trio is imperfect.
responses.response: I share his view of the originality and I ranked it third. The difficulty is the one we both name: Hegemann and Nagel showed that channelrhodopsin is a light-gated channel, Boyden and Deisseroth made it work in neurons, and Bamberg and Miesenboeck are left out of any trio. I would resist treating it as an equal alternative to B042 because it is a tool that enables discovery rather than a discovery about physiology, but as a second-choice configuration I think a Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel prize is defensible.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide over the Habener group is as clear as the shortlist suggests, since I rely on my recollection of that history.
Whether the committee wishes to credit basic physiology alone or to include the drug-development step through Knudsen, and what the choice implies for the citation wording.
Whether B038 (CAR-T) carries a claim comparable to B029 once the omission of Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is weighed, which affects which alternative is stronger.
How to weigh a research tool (B029) against a discovery with direct clinical consequence.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and share an institution with several members, but none of the shortlisted discoveries involves my own work or a candidate I have collaborated with, and I do not treat shared affiliation as a conflict.
